props.gloss_en: חלוגלוגות is what the man was scattering, פרפחיני (purslane, per Steinsaltz) -- as Rebbi's maidservant called it
סלסלה (Prov 4:8) is the word for turning over, as the maidservant said to a man turning his hair over: how long will you מסלסל your hair?
יהבך (Ps 55:23) is a load (טונא): Rabba bar bar Chana, carrying a load, was told by an Arab: take your יהב and throw it on my camel
מטאטא (Isa 14:23) is the טאטיתא with which one טאטי's a house, as the maidservant told her friend (a broom and sweeping, per Steinsaltz)
one who read it at intervals has fulfilled his obligation
one who read it with its order transposed has not fulfilled his obligation
R' Mona in R' Yehuda's name: even reading at intervals, if he paused long enough to finish all of it, he goes back to the beginning
the halakha is as R' Mona (on a pause in reading the Megilla)
(entertained) 'long enough to finish all of it' is measured from where he stands to the end
if so, you have given your words over to [varying] measures
Rav Yosef: it is measured from the beginning to the end
the halakha is not as R' Mona
Rav Yosef: hold Rav Beivai's version in your hand
for it is Shmuel who is concerned for an individual's view
a woman awaiting her brother-in-law, whose sister another brother betrothed: in R' Yehuda ben Beteira's name they said, we tell him: wait until your elder brother acts
Shmuel: the halakha is as R' Yehuda ben Beteira
if the scribe omitted letters or verses and the reader read them as a meturgeman translates, he has fulfilled his obligation
if the Megilla has blurred or torn letters: if their trace is visible it is kosher, and if not it is pasul
the blurred-letters baraita speaks of [defects] throughout the whole Megilla
the omission baraita speaks of [omissions] in part of it
a reader who omitted one verse may not read the whole and then that verse, but reads from that verse onward
one who entered the synagogue and found the congregation had read half may not read half with them and then the [first] half, but reads it from its beginning to its end
